o1.biggest_strength: Shows its working, and the maths checks out: 24,000 rush sized from back-orders plus sale week at 2.5x plus a buffer, an exact ₹117.46 lakh total, and the 82%-of-matte-money-to-42%-of-sales critique of the draft.
o1.biggest_mistake: It counts the 6,400 held units as already on hand, so it concludes the top 5 still run out on 1 December and plans a back-order gap that re-cartoning might close; that assumption isn't challenged.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Settle whether held stock adds to the 9,100, and add a single dated day-by-day timeline for the ops lead instead of dates spread across several tables.

o2.biggest_strength: A single dated action calendar the ops lead can run on Monday, plus smart gap tactics (ad pause, per-shade cap, pro pre-order, honest 'back on 9 December' copy that uses Tanvi's 'I'll wait a week').
o2.biggest_mistake: Same held-stock assumption creates a 1 to 8 December gap. Pausing top-5 ads from 16 November gives up sales while stock still exists, and the liquid lipstick leftover (~27,900) doesn't quite reconcile with plain run-rate.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Test whether re-cartoned stock extends cover to the rush arrival, and time the ad pause and cap to a stock trigger rather than day one.

reason: Both fit the cash and fix the hero shades correctly, but Output 2 hands my ops lead a dated calendar and better tactics for the stockout week, in our voice.
